title: A pilot study on optimising base support in parenteral nutrition for patients with intestinal failure
summary:
People with chronic bowel failure are unable to absorb sufficient nutrients, fluids and salts through the bowel and are therefore fed continuously via a vein (parenteral nutrition). Furthermore, bicarbonate – a substance the body uses to buffer acids – is lost through the diseased or shortened bowel. This can lead to acidosis, which is often not detectable in standard blood tests but can, over time, place a strain on the bones, muscles and kidneys. The amount of alkaline substance that should be added to parenteral nutrition has not yet been established.

In this pilot study, we are measuring the amount of acid excreted by the kidneys in the urine of patients receiving parenteral nutrition. Based on this value, the treatment team adjusts the amount of alkaline substances in the parenteral nutrition. We are investigating whether this approach can be implemented in clinical practice and how it affects the acid-base balance. A total of 12 participants will be monitored over a 12-month period. The results will be used to plan a larger study.

interventions.name:
The supplementation of base equivalents in parenteral nutrition is adjusted on the basis of net acid excretion in the urine (NAE):
1. Calculation of the base equivalent deficit:
NAE surplus = Measured 24-hour NAE – 40 mmol/day
2. Adjustment of parenteral base supplementation
New base dose = Prev

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.    Informed consent form provided
2.    Age ≥ 18 years
3.    Presence of chronic bowel failure, defined as the need for long-term parenteral nutrition due to impaired intestinal absorption.
4.    Last bowel resection at least 6 months prior to study participation
5.    Presence of a jejuno-colonic anastomosis or enterostomy (jejunostomy, ileostomy or enterocutaneous fistula)
6.    Home parenteral nutrition on at least 3 days per week over a period of >3 months
7.	Stable parenteral nutrition with no changes of ≥20 per cent per week in terms of volume, macronutrients, sodium or base equivalents for ≥3 months
8.    Average urine output of ≥ 0.75 and ≤ 3.5 L per day
9.    Net urinary acid excretion >70 mmol per day OR <0 mmol per day at screening
Exclusion criteria:
1.    eGFR <30 ml/min/1.73 m²
2.    Initiation of treatment with GLP-2 analogues less than 1 year ago
3.    Reconstructive surgery planned during the study period
4.    More than 2 hospital admissions due to bowel failure within 6 months prior to enrolment in the study (excluding admissions due to (suspected) sepsis associated with a central venous catheter)
5.    History of severe respiratory diseases
6.    Women who are pregnant, breastfeeding or planning a pregnancy
